subject: Performance/SLO follow-up — context window & latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance/SLO follow-up — context window & latency impact

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the demo and the deep dive today. Per our conversation, here's a short recap and the next steps so we can scope a focused benchmark and proposal.

Recap / goals we discussed:
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 250 ms for the common query shape (see details below).
- Streaming requirement: progressive token streaming to the client with first-byte/initial token ideally < 120 ms.
- Typical throughput/concurrency: steady concurrency around 30 concurrent requests per region, with short bursts up to ~60; expected steady-state throughput ~200–300 RPS across shard(s).
- Context window: most requests are ~2k tokens of history + user prompt; ~10% of traffic can be long transcripts up to ~8k tokens; near-zero usage of 32k+.
- Max output tokens: usually 200–400 tokens, occasionally up to 800 for long summaries.

Primary concerns you raised:
- How much does increasing the context window (2k -> 8k) impact p95 latency?
- How does streaming change the observed SLOs vs non-streaming endpoints?
- Recommendations to hit the SLO while keeping cost predictable (batching, KV caching, reserved capacity).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share 3 representative payloads (one short, one medium, one long transcript) and a daytime peak profile for concurrency (sample window: 10 minutes with peak RPS).
2) We run a targeted benchmark on our Dedicated test pool that mirrors the requested concurrency and context shapes (we'll include both cold and warm KV cache runs).
3) We'll return a short technical report with p50/p95/p99 numbers, streaming first-byte times, and recommended config (model variant, quantization, autoscale settings).

I've attached a one-page draft SLO doc for your review and an internal benchmark extract — these are preliminary but align with what we discussed.

Thanks — if that plan looks good I can schedule the benchmark as early as next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Performance_SLO_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCo Procurement <procurement@finco.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance/SLO follow-up — context window & latency impact

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side so your benchmark matches production shapes: 

- Context distribution: ~80% under 2k tokens, ~15% in 2k–8k, ~5% >8k (very rare).
- Outputs: ~70% under 250 tokens; ~25% 250–500 tokens; ~5% up to 800 tokens.
- Concurrency: steady 30 concurrent at peak, but we see short 3–5 minute bursts up to 75 concurrent.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is a hard requirement for the UI — we need progressive updates and a visible first token within ~150 ms ideally.
- Caching: we have repeated prefixes for some workflows (legal transcripts). Any prefix-caching hit would materially help.

Specific asks: 
1) Can you include both streaming and non-streaming measurements in the benchmark (first-byte and end-of-response)?
2) For the 8k cases, please show both cold-cache and 100% warm-cache numbers if possible.
3) Rough cost delta if we recommend a Reserved/Dedicated capacity vs pure on-demand hosting (ballpark is fine).

Happy to send sample payloads today — will attach anonymized transcripts. Also please cc your engineering contact if we need to coordinate on packet captures or network details.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of AI Integrations, FinCo
samantha.lee@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance/SLO follow-up — context window & latency impact

Samantha — perfect, thanks for the distribution and the confirmation on streaming. We're good to proceed.

Quick notes from our infra benching team (high-level, attached detailed CSV):
- Baseline (model: redwood-2-small, Dedicated test pool, single-GPU profile):
  - 512-in / 256-out (non-streaming): p50 ~85 ms, p95 ~180 ms, p99 ~340 ms at steady concurrency 30 (warm KV).
  - 512-in / 256-out (streaming): first-byte p50 ~45 ms, first-byte p95 ~95 ms; end-of-stream p95 ~160–200 ms.
- 8k-in / 256-out (cold KV): p95 increases to ~450–650 ms depending on KV cache hit rate and model variant (memory paging and KV copy overhead are the drivers).
- 8k-in / 256-out (warm KV with prefix cache hits ~20%): p95 drops to ~300–420 ms.

Key mitigations we recommend to hit your 250 ms p95 target for common traffic:
- Encourage prefix caching for repeated transcript prefixes (we can pin common prefixes into the KV store).
- Cap max_output_tokens for latency-sensitive endpoints (reducing max_output from 800 to 400 can shave ~50–120 ms on end-to-end in our tests).
- Use streaming to improve perceived latency (first-byte targets are considerably lower than end-of-stream).
- Consider a Dedicated reserved pool sized for your peak concurrency bursts (this avoids cold-starts and reduces variance).
- Model selection: offer a slightly smaller low-latency variant for short/medium contexts and a larger model for long-context batch processing (offload very long summaries to async pipelines).

Attachments: latency CSV with breakdowns (cold/warm, streaming first-byte, end-to-end) and a draft SLO doc that maps behaviors to recommended SLA language.

If you approve, we'll run the benchmark using your anonymized payloads and share a single-page deliverable plus recommended quota/capacity numbers and cost ballpark (Reserved vs on-demand). Proposed window: Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks — looping in Rachel to coordinate the benchmark scheduling and Connor for infra sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
[Attachments: Performance_SLO_Draft_v2.pdf, Latency_Benchmarks_8k_16k.csv]

I'll sync with Rachel Monday to lock down the exact test config before we run the benchmark.
